study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To use normative modeling to assess the effect of pharmacological treatment on the brain state of patients with schizophrenia, and to investigate the relationship between brain deviations and clinical symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: General linear models and Pearson's correlations of the deviation profiles on bSCZ/aSCZ and clinical PANSS scores were conducted to explore the relationships between clinical symptom improvement and changes in dynamic FC patterns gaged with the deviation Z-scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study found that patients with milder symptoms at baseline were more likely to show a normalization trend in brain characteristics after treatment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Patients were divided into two groups based on deviation changes after treatment: a 'normalization' group and a 'deviated' group. The normalization group had milder positive and overall symptoms at baseline. Baseline depressive and overall symptoms could predict the deviation of brain networks after treatment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: This study is the first to use a normative model to assess the effects of pharmacological treatment on brain changes in patients with schizophrenia.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small sample size, potential bias from using 10-fold cross-validation, and potential confounding effects of medication.
